page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, with read speeds of 51.54 GB/sec and write speeds of 38.79 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads are relatively weak. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instructions, yielding average performance in Passmark encryption tests.

The c2d-standard-4 offers a dedicated hardware profile that avoids the CPU resource contention typical of shared-core budget instances, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring predictable single-threaded execution. However, its lower multi-core scaling and weak performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput represent notable tradeoffs. This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, single-threaded batch processing, or small-scale text processing workloads rather than highly parallelized database or high-throughput web serving applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with multithreading, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests, though multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth for small blocks fall into the bottom 25%. The instance delivers average performance in encryption and large-block memory transfers. Given its dedicated resource allocation and moderate memory-to-vCPU ratio, the c2d-standard-4 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution over highly parallel processing. It is best suited for lightweight batch processing, single-threaded applications, and moderate general-purpose computing tasks.
